purpose: Inventory of every problem the framework currently has that prevents the 'framework improves FM model outputs' paper claim from being supported by direct experimental evidence. Each entry has a unique ID, severity, the experiment it blocks, and a one-line fix sketch. Old implementation-task list archived at todo.json.bak.

problems.title: FlowMol3 partial-fidelity (444/475 GVP graph-conv tensors skipped)
problems.description: FlowMol3 Lightning ckpt has 475 tensors. The harness reconstructs the embedding + readout path (token tables, scalar_embedding, edge_embedding, node_output_head, to_edge_logits) from the real pretrained tensors, but the 444 GVP graph-conv layers / node_position_updaters / edge_updaters tensors are NOT applied because dgl/flowmol have no Python 3.12 wheel. The resulting velocity field is trained-marginal-only, not graph-conditioned. Validity sits at 12.5% / 6.25% (paper reports >90%). The baseline vs framework numbers (validity -0.0625, QED +0.317, SA +1.18, logP +7.93) come from this partial model and are NOT paper-comparable.
problems.fix_sketch: (a) write GVP equivalent in pure torch (no DGL); or (b) downgrade Python to 3.11 + install dgl; or (c) replace FlowMol3 with a different SOTA 3D-mol FM (e.g. DiffDock-style DiT) that has pure-torch reference.
problems.evidence: tools/run_sota_flowmol3_v2_adapter_experiment.py smoke run output: validity 0.125 (baseline) vs 0.0625 (framework); commit 6145739; module docstring of _build_flowmol3_velocity_module in adaptive_reflow/adapters/flowmol3_v2_adapter.py.

research_findings.root_cause: Two independent defects compound: (1) dgl==1.1.x and the flowmol package have no cp312 wheel on PyPI, so the published equivariant graph-conv net (444 GVP tensor blocks across node_position_updaters / edge_updaters / conv_layers) cannot be instantiated; (2) the harness keeps the embedding + readout path on real pretrained tensors but bypasses the GVP core, so the velocity field becomes per-token-marginal conditioned on type/charge/edge tables rather than per-graph-conditioned. The adapter docstring in adaptive_reflow/adapters/flowmol3_v2_adapter.py is explicit that validity collapse is a direct consequence of skipping the conv path. The 444 skipped tensors are documented in the harness's summary.json model_metadata block (gvp_tensors_skipped=444, checkpoint_tensors_loaded=475).
research_findings.plan: Pick option (a) -- pure-torch GVP reimplementation -- because options (b) and (c) either regress the dev environment (py3.12 -> 3.11) or replace a paper-comparable 3D-mol FM with a different model class. Steps: (1) port the 7 GVP message-passing layers from the FlowMol3 reference to pure torch (no DGL heterograph; use dense neighbor gather + scatter); (2) wire the new layers into _build_flowmol3_velocity_module so the full 475 tensors flow; (3) re-run tools/run_sota_flowmol3_v2_adapter_experiment.py smoke + a 100-sample baseline-vs-framework run; (4) compare validity against the published >90% reference. Fallback if (a) exceeds 2 weeks: swap to option (c) (DiffDock-style DiT) and document in paper Section 4.2.
files: docs/r17-survey/mol-comparison.md (regenerate FlowMol3 row with real validity)
risks: Pure-torch GVP reimplementation may diverge from the published ckpt by enough that downstream QED/SA/logP/FCD metrics shift; even if validity recovers, the comparison numbers in mol-comparison.md must be re-baselined.

Approx 7 GVP layers x ~50 lines each = ~350 LoC, plus careful equivariance preservation (rotation/reflection equivariance of node+edge updates); a bug in equivariance will silently degrade geometry-dependent metrics.
FCD still depends on data/geom_drugs_reference.smi being vendored; the partial-fidelity run already showed FCD=NaN because the reference is absent. Fixing GVP does not fix FCD.
research_findings.time_estimate: 5-10 working days for a careful pure-torch port + re-verification; longer if equivariance tests need to be added from scratch.
research_findings.api_alignment_findings: P-01 [L] in docs/r17-survey/sota-adapter-audit.md notes FlowMol3V2Adapter lacks the inject_forward_noise hook (the legacy flowmol3.py placeholder still has it). Once GVP is back, this is a second parallel fix in the same file.

problems.title: ProtBFN + AbBFN baseline runs uniform reference, not trained-model single-pass
problems.blocks: ProtBFN + AbBFN paper-parity perplexity comparison; the only 'baseline' number reported (perplexity=22) is a uniform-distribution reference, not the trained BFN model evaluated single-pass
problems.description: tools/run_sota_protbfn_abbfn_adapter_experiment.py reports baseline_perplexity_uniform_ref=22 (uniform over 20 amino acids) instead of the trained BFN model run for baseline_nfe=250 ODE steps. This makes the baseline-vs-framework comparison nonsensical: framework trained model with 8 BFN steps vs uniform distribution. The proper baseline is the trained ProtBFN/AbBFN model run for the same NFE budget as the framework's total budget.
problems.fix_sketch: Replace baseline_perplexity_uniform_ref with a single-pass run: call ProtBFNAbBFNAdapter.solve_ode directly for --baseline-nfe steps using a fresh build_initial_state + sample, then compute mean per-sequence perplexity. Compare against the framework's N round-multi-pass result with the same total NFE.
problems.status: closed-verify-pending (P-02 trained-baseline wiring is workflow A phase 4; recommend flip to closed once workflow A emits a trained-model single-pass baseline perplexity)
problems.evidence: tools/run_sota_protbfn_abbfn_adapter_experiment.py baseline_perplexity_uniform_ref=22 (uniform over 22 amino acids, not trained model). P-05 update added --bfn-steps-per-round default 125 = paper parity. Trained-model baseline fix is in flight under workflow A phase 4. docs/r17-survey/prot-comparison.md §3 records current apples-to-oranges comparison.

research_findings.root_cause: tools/run_sota_protbfn_abbfn_adapter_experiment.py builds a baseline_perplexity_uniform_ref by computing -log(1/K) with K=22 (PROTBFN_VOCAB_SIZE). This is a categorical-uniform negative log-likelihood, not a model output. The framework's per-sequence perplexity (679.372 round 0, 643.141 round 1) is a real BFN-trained likelihood at 8 steps; the gap is therefore an apples-to-oranges comparison. The harness never invokes ProtBFNAbBFNAdapter.solve_ode for the baseline arm, so it never compares two trained-model likelihoods at matched NFE.
research_findings.plan: Three-step fix in tools/run_sota_protbfn_abbfn_adapter_experiment.py main(): (1) build a ProtBFNAbBFNAdapter with --mode=protbfn or --mode=abbfn, force_mode='auto' OFF; (2) call adapter.build_initial_state(...) -> adapter.solve_ode(state, condition, seed=42, n_steps=baseline_nfe) for one full ODE pass and compute mean per-token categorical log-likelihood against the produced logits; (3) record baseline_perplexity_trained_model and paired_delta_perplexity_trained_vs_framework. Add a CLI flag --baseline-mode=trained|uniform (default trained; uniform kept as a reference sanity check).
files: adaptive_reflow/adapters/protbfn_abbfn_adapter.py (verify solve_ode exposes per-step logits; if not, add an evaluator hook)
risks: A trained-model single-pass baseline at NFE=250 may produce a perplexity that is *worse* than uniform (the framework's 8-step run is already 661.256); if so the paper claim still fails, but at least the comparison is apples-to-apples.

Current CPU numpy+torch sampler may diverge significantly from the JAX reference; P-05 already warns that paper-parity requires GPU-equivalent sampler. Fixing P-02 alone is necessary but not sufficient for paper parity.
Wall-clock for the trained baseline at NFE=250 may be 30-60 min per run (current 8-step run takes ~3 min); need to budget that into CI.
research_findings.time_estimate: 1-2 days for the trained-baseline wiring + 1 day for the rerun + comparison doc regeneration.

problems.title: Lumina-Image 2.0 FID is placeholder (no MJHQ-30K reference stats)
problems.blocks: Lumina paper-parity FID/CLIPScore against published numbers (GenEval 0.73, MJHQ-30K FID)
problems.description: tools/run_sota_lumina_image_2_0_experiment.py computes FID against mu/sigma computed from the generated images themselves (rank-deficient 2048-d covariance on 8 samples), yielding placeholder FID ~6e25. CLIPScore NaN (HF offline). Without MJHQ-30K or COCO-30K reference stats, no meaningful FID is possible.
problems.fix_sketch: (a) download MJHQ-30K (huggingface.co/datasets/playgroundai/MJHQ-30K, ~12GB) and compute reference mu/sigma via canonical-pytorch-fid's make_custom_stats(); or (b) use the openai/clip-vit-large-patch14 model (online) for CLIPScore.
problems.evidence: tools/run_sota_lumina_image_2_0_experiment.py smoke run output: baseline_fid=6.259e+25, framework_fid=2.496e+25; commit 6145739; placeholder_reference_note field.

research_findings.root_cause: tools/extract_inception_features is called twice: once on the 8 generated images per arm to compute the 'reference' mu/sigma, once on the generated images themselves. With only 8 samples in a 2048-d InceptionV3 pool3 space, the reference covariance is rank-deficient and the FID value explodes to ~1e25. CLIPScore returns NaN because tools/run_image_eval.py uses openai/clip-vit-base-patch32 from HF, which requires online access that is blocked in the audit sandbox. Both metrics are placeholders, not paper-comparable.
research_findings.plan: (1) Download MJHQ-30K from huggingface.co/datasets/playgroundai/MJHQ-30K (~12GB at 1024x1024) via snapshot_download once network is available; (2) run tools/extract_inception_features over the 30K reference set to produce data/lumina_image_2_0_inception_stats.npz with mu/sigma; (3) wire tools/run_sota_lumina_image_2_0_experiment.py to load data/lumina_image_2_0_inception_stats.npz and compute real FID; (4) replace openai/clip-vit-base-patch32 with openai/clip-vit-large-patch14 (online) or fall back to an offline-cached CLIP; (5) re-run with at least 256 generated images per arm so the InceptionV3 covariance is well-conditioned.
files: tools/run_sota_lumina_image_2_0_experiment.py (load reference stats from data/ instead of computing from generated)
tools/run_image_eval.py (swap CLIP model + graceful offline fallback)
docs/r17-survey/img-comparison.md (regenerate Lumina row with real FID)
risks: MJHQ-30K download is 12GB and gated by HF auth in some regions; if blocked, fall back to COCO-30K 256x256 subset (~6GB).
Increasing samples per arm from 8 to 256 will increase Lumina wall-clock by ~32x; current 4.946s baseline + 2.53s framework -> ~158s + 81s, still tractable on cuda:1.
If CLIP stays offline, CLIPScore remains NaN; that is acceptable as long as FID is real (paper Section 4 reports both but FID is the primary metric).
research_findings.time_estimate: 1 day for download + feature extraction + harness wiring + rerun.

problems.title: HiDream-I1-Dev eval layer CUDA device-ordinal mismatch
problems.description: HiDream samples generated on cuda:1 (RTX 5090) because the 17B transformer at bf16 (~34GB) exceeds 32GB VRAM, but the eval layer (tools/run_image_eval.py) is invoked without the same --device, so FID/CLIPScore runs on cuda:0 (default) and finds no samples there. PNG samples are real and on disk; only the metric pipeline fails.
problems.fix_sketch: Pass --device cuda:1 all the way through to tools/run_image_eval.py; or have the harness invoke extract_inception_features(images, device='cuda:1') explicitly; or load samples into the eval device before computing features.
problems.status: closed-verify-pending (HiDream device-ordinal fix verified end-to-end previously per task #341; FID 9.888e+25 produced on re-score confirms wiring; recommend flip to closed once workflow A re-scores with torch env)
problems.evidence: tools/run_image_eval.py --device propagation fixed (task #341); data/hidream_i1_inception_stats.npz regenerated with IMAGENET1K_V1 weights (mu mean 0.328, max 0.624); HiDream harness supervisor PID 388517 was running on cuda:1; subsequent re-score confirmed real finite FID. Empirical per-round trajectory pending torch install (workflow A phase 1).

research_findings.root_cause: tools/run_sota_hidream_i1_experiment.py auto-falls-back to enable_sequential_cpu_offload(device='cuda:1') because the 17B DiT at bf16 = 34GB exceeds the 32GB VRAM on cuda:0. After generation, the harness writes PNGs to data/hidream_i1/samples/. The subsequent eval call to tools/run_image_eval.py defaults device='cuda:0', which loads InceptionV3/CLIP on cuda:0 but finds no samples on cuda:0 (they live on cuda:1). InceptionV3's load_image_batch enumerates samples by device placement and returns zero, yielding NaN FID/CLIPScore.
research_findings.plan: Three-line fix: (1) add --device flag to tools/run_image_eval.py (currently hardcoded cuda:0); (2) thread --device from run_sota_hidream_i1_experiment.py into the run_image_eval subprocess call; (3) verify with a smoke run that FID is finite (not NaN). Optional: also load data/hidream_i1_inception_stats.npz so FID is computed against a real reference rather than placeholder-vs-placeholder.
files: data/hidream_i1_inception_stats.npz (new; optional but recommended for real FID)
risks: If cuda:1 is not always the offload device (e.g. another machine has 48GB on cuda:0), the --device flag must be propagated from the generation device rather than hardcoded; implement via an env var FLOWA_HIDREAM_DEVICE that the harness sets before invoking eval.

Loading InceptionV3 on cuda:1 will conflict with the offloaded DiT if both are active simultaneously; the eval must run *after* the DiT has been moved off cuda:1 (already the case in the harness's sequential pipeline).
research_findings.time_estimate: 0.5 day for the device-arg wiring + smoke rerun.

problems.title: ProtBFN/AbBFN 8 BFN steps too few for paper-parity
problems.blocks: Reproducing paper-reported perplexity (ProtBFN perplexity < native, AbBFN perplexity < naive baseline)
problems.description: With --baseline-nfe=250 and --n-rounds=2 the framework only spends ~8 BFN steps per round (round budget = 250/2 = 125 total, divided by chain length). Per-sequence perplexity 661 (ProtBFN) is WORSE than uniform reference (22). Paper uses ~250 BFN steps in a single pass. Either baseline_nfe should be much higher or n_rounds should be lower with more steps per round.
problems.fix_sketch: Run a single-pass baseline at the same total NFE as the framework's total budget; OR increase per-round BFN steps to ~125 with --n-rounds=2; OR document that paper-parity requires GPU-equivalent sampler (current sampler is CPU numpy+torch).
problems.status: closed-verify-pending (--bfn-steps-per-round default 125 = paper parity with --baseline-nfe=250; total FlowA NFE budget = 2 rounds x 125 = 250; recommend flip to closed once trained-model baseline at matched NFE lands)
problems.evidence: tools/run_sota_protbfn_abbfn_adapter_experiment.py harness updated; docs/r17-survey/prot-comparison.md header note records P-05 update. CPU numpy+torch sampler-to-JAX swap still open (P-05 research_findings.risks).

research_findings.root_cause: tools/run_sota_protbfn_abbfn_adapter_experiment.py divides the total NFE budget (250) by chain_length (32) and rounds (~16), yielding ~8 effective BFN steps per round. The paper's trained-model perplexity uses ~250 BFN steps in a single pass, so the 8-step approximation is far too coarse. Additionally the BFN sampler is implemented in numpy+torch on CPU, which diverges from the JAX reference sampler used in the paper.
research_findings.plan: (1) Once P-02 is fixed (trained-model baseline), increase --n-rounds=2 to --n-rounds=1 with --baseline-nfe=250 so both arms get the full 250 BFN steps; (2) compare trained-single-pass-250 vs trained-multi-pass-250 framework output at matched total NFE; (3) if CPU sampler still diverges, swap to JAX sampler via adaptive_reflow/adapters/protbfn_abbfn_jax_loader.py (the loader already exists but is only used for weight loading); (4) re-run, document the perplexity gap in docs/r17-survey/prot-comparison.md.
files: tools/run_sota_protbfn_abbfn_adapter_experiment.py (change --n-rounds default + ensure trained baseline uses 250 steps)
adaptive_reflow/adapters/protbfn_abbfn_adapter.py (verify solver dispatches JAX sampler when available)
risks: Even with trained-model baseline at matched NFE, if framework perplexity > baseline perplexity, the paper claim fails. That result is still informative (it disproves the claim at this NFE), but the paper text must acknowledge it.
CPU sampler-to-JAX swap may shift perplexity by ~10-30 perplexity units even at matched NFE due to floating-point + sampler choice; document this as a known limitation.
research_findings.time_estimate: 2-3 days (1 day for harness flag changes + rerun, 1-2 days if JAX sampler swap is needed).

problems.title: HiDream-I1-Dev text_encoder_4 (Llama-3.1-8B) missing from snapshot
problems.blocks: HiDream full-text-encoder chain fidelity; T5-only fallback may degrade prompt fidelity
problems.description: HiDream-I1-Dev HF snapshot is missing the Llama-3.1-8B text_encoder_4 weights (likely intentionally pruned in the Dev variant or a HF upload miss). Harness uses a _StubLlama zero-output nn.Module + _StubTokenizer passthrough, so the DiT residual only flows through the T5-XXL branch.
problems.fix_sketch: (a) git clone the full HiDream-I1-Dev repo (not just snapshot_download from HF); (b) request gated Llama-3.1-8B weights separately; or (c) explicitly document in paper Section 4 that HiDream Dev uses T5-XXL-only conditioning, not the 3-encoder full version.
problems.evidence: tools/run_sota_hidream_i1_experiment.py smoke run output: 'text_encoder_4 (Llama-3.1-8B) missing from local snapshot; _StubLlama zero-output nn.Module + _StubTokenizer passthrough substitute'; commit 6145739.

research_findings.root_cause: HiDream-I1-Dev is a 17B-parameter MoE DiT with three text encoders: T5-XXL (encoder_1), CLIP-L (encoder_2), and Llama-3.1-8B (encoder_4). The HF snapshot_download call only fetches the DiT and T5 weights; the Llama-3.1-8B weights are gated behind a Meta license that HF cannot redistribute. The harness falls back to a zero-output nn.Module for the Llama branch, so the encoder_4 contribution to the DiT cross-attention is exactly zero.
research_findings.plan: Two viable paths. Path A (paper integrity): explicitly document in paper Section 4.3 that HiDream-Dev on this rig uses T5-XXL-only conditioning because the Llama-3.1-8B weights are gated; this is a defensible scope decision. Path B (full fidelity): apply for Meta Llama-3.1-8B access, download weights into data/hidream_i1/llama-3.1-8b/, and replace _StubLlama with the real transformer; verify that prompt fidelity (CLIPScore against prompt embeddings) recovers. Path A is cheaper and matches the current behaviour; Path B is needed only if the paper claim hinges on full-fidelity 3-encoder HiDream.
files: adaptive_reflow/adapters/hidream_i1.py (no change for Path A; Path B requires _StubLlama -> real Llama swap)
docs/r17-survey/img-comparison.md (note T5-only conditioning in HiDream-Dev row)
risks: Path B introduces a 16GB Llama-3.1-8B weight file plus VRAM contention with the DiT on cuda:1; sequential CPU offload must be re-verified.

Even with real Llama weights, paper-comparable CLIPScore requires the encoder_4 contribution to be wired into the DiT's cross-attention; the harness currently routes encoder_4 outputs into a zero stub, so wiring is required, not just weight loading.
research_findings.time_estimate: 0.5 day for Path A (doc-only). 2-3 days for Path B (weights + wiring + re-verification).

problems.title: No direct evidence the framework improves outputs (RE-FRAMED: gated on synthetic oracle P-13..P-17 + hyperparameter-free principle P-18)
problems.blocks: Paper's core claim ('framework improves FM model outputs') is currently unproven
problems.description: STRATEGIC RE-FRAMING (r17-post): User insight: 'core conflict is not only math alignment gap; algorithm core itself may have bugs; testing on real SOTA too early masks both'. P-08's old dependency (P-01..P-04) addresses SOTA-side defects but does NOT address whether the framework's algorithm core (Scheduler/Blender/MergeOperator/Materializer) is even correct on known ground truth. Evidence pointing to algorithm-side bugs: (a) ProtBFN per-round perplexity 1.761 → 1.813 (3% worse) under framework schedule despite arm-level 7.1% improvement -- per-round-vs-arm divergence is scheduler/blender pathology, not alignment; (b) FlowMol3 paper metrics ALL regressed (validity -0.0625, atom_stability regressed, mol_stability regressed) -- consistent with materializer round-trip losing atom-type information; (c) HiDream FID +27.32 worse but CLIPScore +0.43 better simultaneously -- two metrics disagreeing is internal-framework inconsistency, not just alignment. ADDITIONAL INSIGHT (2026-09-01 15:10): framework hyperparameters (memory_fraction, alpha_grad, eps_threshold, n_rounds, etc.) should be DERIVED from paper quantities A_g/B_g/C_g/e_rho and mathematical theory, not hand-written. Current hand-written defaults (memory_fraction=m=?, alpha_grad=0.5, tolerance=1e-9) are the silent-source-of-many-bugs hypothesis. NEW DEPENDENCY: P-08 now gates on P-13..P-17 (synthetic oracle) AND P-18 (hyperparameter-free principle). If P-16 (framework passes synthetic oracle) or P-19 (hyperparameter-free principle validates) fails, the framework has bugs to fix BEFORE more SOTA investment. SOTA-side fixes P-01..P-06 are NOT sufficient and may even be misleading.
problems.fix_sketch: Closed when: (a) P-13 (2D Gaussian mix oracle) + P-14 (algorithm unit tests) + P-15 (synthetic image ground truth) + P-16 (framework passes synthetic oracle) + P-19 (hyperparameter-free principle validated) all green; (b) P-01..P-06 SOTA-side defects closed AND per-round FID trajectories from P-16 validation match oracle predictions. problems.description: pytest reports a single unrelated failure: tests/test_adapters/test_mnist_fm_train.py::test_train_smoke_decreases_loss throws urllib.error.URLError SSL: UNEXPECTED_EOF_WHILE_READING because the sandbox's HTTPS connection to the MNIST mirror is broken. research_findings.root_cause: tests/test_adapters/test_mnist_fm_train.py::test_train_smoke_decreases_loss calls torchvision.datasets.MNIST which downloads from yann.lecun.com/flux/exdb/mnist/. The sandbox's TLS handshake to that mirror fails with UNEXPECTED_EOF_WHILE_READING. The test is unrelated to the r17 SOTA workflow (it tests a tiny MNIST FM training run), but it fails every verify phase, masking CI signal.
research_findings.plan: Cheapest fix: add a pytest fixture that monkeypatches torchvision.datasets.MNIST to point at a local mirror (data/mnist/ or a cached tarball). Robust fix: vendor the 4 MNIST .gz files into data/mnist/raw/ at test-collection time and have the fixture check there first. Skip-fix: wrap the download in pytest.importorskip('torch') with a try/except SSL guard; only skip in offline mode.
files: tests/test_adapters/test_mnist_fm_train.py (add a fixture that points at data/mnist/ first)
conftest.py or new tests/conftest.py (mark offline-only tests with a guard)
risks: Vendoring 50MB of MNIST into the repo bloats the repo; consider git-lfs or a Makefile target that downloads once.

research_findings.resolution: Applied option (c) local-mirror approach. _REPO_ROOT/data/mnist_fm_train_cache/MNIST/raw/ contains the 4 vendored MNIST .gz files (train + t10k images + labels); tests/test_adapters/test_mnist_fm_train.py documents the SSL fragility in its module docstring and uses contextlib.redirect_stdout to swallow the torchvision 'downloaded' progress bar. issues.summary: Lacks inject_forward_noise hook; runner's hasattr fallback still emits FORWARD_NOISE_INJECTED but adapter-side native state not threaded.
state_shape=(3,) is a 1-atom degenerate prior placeholder for the heterogeneous (x, a, c, e) native state.
